title: Data by Matthew Libby at the Lucille Lortel Theatre #datatheplay #kar...
transcript: When I tell you this play had me completely on edge, I don't just mean on the edge of my seat. Data is a new play by Matthew Libby following a young software engineer grappling with a big moral dilemma about the tech company he's working at. The roughly 100-minute single act almost overflows with suspense and reveals, each one more stomach-churning than the last. I won't give away any specifics, but it's thematically very timely and the project discussed in the play is absolutely chilling. The lean cast of four is great, the writing and direction are sharp and realistic, and the aesthetic of the production is appropriately sterile, in a dystopian kind of way. It feels like it should be science fiction, but what makes the play so impactful is knowing that there are versions of this story playing out as we speak. I think it's great that we're seeing more stories around the intersection between technology and ethics, as it's certainly an area of research and discussion that is consistently outpaced by technological advancement itself. I would totally recommend this piece — it's educational, thought provoking, and plain old entertaining theatre. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
